sections.name: summary
sections.value: Cursor's IDE agent edits files with Write and StrReplace, but cursor-adapter.ts only extracts file evidence from ApplyPatch string payloads. Those edits emit zero file events, so attribution silently reports 0% agent on code an agent wrote entirely — a well-formed report with a confident wrong number, not an error. This adds both tool vocabularies behind a closed registry, and a read-side honesty counter that fires when write-shaped calls yielded no file events, so the next Cursor rename is loud instead of silent.

sections.name: goals
value: Cursor Write/StrReplace edits produce file events with correct per-file line and byte deltas
A Cursor session's agent-contribution share computes correctly end to end, not as 0%
Both tool vocabularies coexist — ApplyPatch never deprecated, since this is a Cursor version rename not a surface split
A future Cursor tool rename surfaces as a named gap rather than a silent zero

sections.name: non_goals
value: Fixing the Claude adapter's Map.set churn loss — logged, not worked
Diagnosing the win=0..0 capture stall — plan-070 class, judged only after this lands
V4A 'Move to:' rename handling — dropped to follow-up, no local specimen exercises it
Changing the segment wire version — additionalProperties:false pins 2.7, so the counter is read-side by construction

value.claim: A Write tool_use yields one 'written' file event whose lines_added equals the content line count and whose bytes_added is a real UTF-8 encode (proven with a multibyte body, so a char-count implementation fails)
A StrReplace tool_use yields one 'edited' file event with an old-to-new multiset delta; unchanged context lines contribute nothing and a pure reorder yields zero
ApplyPatch extraction is unchanged — the existing golden fixture 2026-08-03-applypatch-textstat passes byte-identical
A path touched by Write then StrReplace repeatedly keeps every delta via array-push (not Map.set), so the specimen's lib.test.mjs x6 and cli.mjs x3 sum rather than overwrite
cursor-object-write.test.ts passes UNMODIFIED — its two controls prove the adapter sees both calls, isolating the extraction gate as sole cause

When write-shaped calls occurred and zero file events were extracted, SessionExport.summary.degraded carries an 'event_skipped:' prefixed marker, so the envelope downgrades by construction with no change to acts/telemetry.ts
The tool registry is closed: any tool name absent from it classifies as unknown and fires the counter, so the next rename is loud
The Cursor-scoping predicate is pinned to the corpus by a test asserting both real fixtures carry harness 'cursor-agent' — a scope gate that silently matches nothing is this defect one level up
Both must-NOT-fire controls hold: 2026-06-25-checks-walkthrough (write-free, also guards registry completeness) and 2026-08-03-applypatch-textstat
A synthetic unit test proves lowercase drive-letter confinement ('c:\repo\src\x.ts' becomes repo-relative); the scrubbed fixture cannot carry this because scrubbing rebases the drive letter away
A planted secret in contents / old_string / new_string never appears in the serialized segment (AC-04 privacy boundary)
Every new assertion is proven non-vacuous — it goes RED when its branch is removed
docs/how/measuring-ai-contribution.md's blind-spot list names the new write tools, closing the loop its own warning opened

A new golden fixture minted from the scrubbed IDE-agent specimen reproduces 432 lines added and 22 removed across 14 events over 6 distinct paths, computed with the repo's OWN computeFileDelta/writtenDelta (a multiset diff, so StrReplace anchor lines present on both sides cancel). The reporting agent's simulator gives 438 - a reimplementation, not this repo's semantics. The golden must never be tuned to match it.
